page.layout: One printed page (page 39). One column of running text, with a narrow margin of cropped notes on the left. Running head at top. Catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.l: quod libros illos aut Episcopos tangeret, quo re-
sponso, delusos, ac vana spe lactatos, cum se cerne-
rent deputati, nomine omnium Regni civium, qui-
bus haec res cordi fuit, protestationem contra Sena-
tum regium parant, seque, pacificis omnibus mediis
frustra tentatis, Ecclesiis deesse non posse declarant,
si quis porro exoriretur in prosecutione causae hu-
jus tumultus, soli Senatui ob negatam justitiam im-
putandus esset.. Quod cum Senatui regio subole-
ret, nec ignoraret, quam proxima fumo esset flam-
ma, Episcopis (ut fertur) primum monitis, ut se
à Senatu pro tempore subducerent; deputatis com-
parendi licentiam concedit, qui quia sciebant diffi-
cilem esse in Senatum ingressum, ante januam Pal-
latii Dalkethensis (quo in oppido tum cogebantur)
praestolabantur, ut Senatoribus saltem egredienti-
bus protestationem insinuarent.
Vbi comparuere Deputati in Senatu, omnium
nomine verba fecit nobilis Dominus de Lowdon, Vice-
comes Avrensis, singulari facundia & animi constantia
explicabat, quid ab initio libellorum supplicum
Senatui exhibitorum actum fuisset, quae ipsorum
causae, quam modeste ac patienter Regis optimi
clementiam expectassent, & quorum artibus quod
ea non fruantur factum sit, paratos se contra Epi-
scopos actionem instituere, institutamque prosequi,
qua se probaturos suscipiunt eosdem gravissimo-
rum criminum reos esse, idque sub capitum, hono-
rum, fortunarum suarum periculo, & poena, si in
probatione deficient, aut coram aequis judicibus
causa cadent, aequitatem itaque postulare, ut a Se-
natu regio excluderentur Episcopi, donec de
ipso- rum innocentia constiterit: esse absurdum, eosdem
habere judices & adversarios, denique. Senatores
regios obtestatur, ut procrastinationibus omnibus
posthabitis, tandem aliquando aliquid hac in causa

page.notes: The left margin is cropped at the scan edge: most marginal notes are only fragments and are transcribed as far as legible, with [?]. Their exact words cannot be recovered. Paragraph 2 margin fragments are especially uncertain and their line positions are approximate. The bottom line "facc-" is the catchword, and "C 4" is the signature. The running head is "IN REGNO SCOT."; the year 1637 is not included. Long s is written as s throughout; the scan's "f" in "fponfo" and "fruftra" was read as s.
